haiku-low.q1: A pull request builds and runs unit tests only, with no push and no deploy. A merge to main starts a run that can deploy.
haiku-low.q2: Staging and production both deploy registry.internal/shop-api:<SHA>, built once in step 1. Nothing is rebuilt after the tests.
haiku-low.q3: An integration test failure retries the whole job once and fails only if the second attempt also fails. A unit test failure fails the run immediately, with no retry.
haiku-low.q4: Staging is rolled back to the tag in SSM /deploy/staging/previous_tag, the tag staging ran before this deploy. The rollback reads that SSM value.
haiku-low.q5: Only release-approvers may approve, and the approver must not be the commit author. If nobody approves within 72 hours, the run expires and nothing goes to production.
haiku-low.q6: In AWS SSM Parameter Store, at /deploy/<env>/current_tag and previous_tag. deploy.sh writes them after a staging or production rollout succeeds. The canary is never recorded.
haiku-low.q7: Stable keeps running its old image, and canary-off scales the canary to 0. Tags are not written. The migration stays applied, which is safe because it works with the previous image.
haiku-low.q8: The older run is cancelled at its next checkpoint, without an announced failure, once a newer run passes smoke tests. A run already holding the production lock is never cancelled.
haiku-low.q9: Outside the window it holds no lock and checks the clock every minute until inside the window. While another production deploy holds the lock, it waits in line, then rechecks the window.
haiku-low.q10: The canary's 5xx ratio is read every 30 s for 15 minutes by the pipeline via a Prometheus query. Any reading above 1%, or a failed query, fails the run and triggers canary-off.
haiku-low.q12: No automatic rollback runs after a failed stable rollout, because tags were not written and rollback would target the wrong tag. In production, a person must check the stable deployment.

sonnet.q1: A pull request runs build and unit tests only (no push, no deploy, failures not announced). A push to main (a merge) starts a run that can deploy; tags and PRs do not.
sonnet.q2: Both deploy the single image registry.internal/shop-api:<SHA>, built once in step 1. Nothing is rebuilt later.
sonnet.q3: Integration tests: the whole job is retried once with a fresh Postgres container; the run fails only if the second attempt fails. Unit tests: no retry; failure fails the run. Failure is announced in #deploys and locks are released.
sonnet.q4: Pipeline runs deploy.sh rollback staging, which sets staging back to SSM previous_tag (the tag staging ran before this run's deploy), writes it as current_tag, then fails the run. The image is found via SSM /deploy/staging/previous_tag.
sonnet.q5: Only members of release-approvers, and not the author of the merged commit (checked after approval; run fails if same). If nobody approves within 72 h, the run expires, announces the expiry, nothing goes to production, and staging stays on that tag.
sonnet.q6: AWS SSM Parameter Store: /deploy/<env>/current_tag and /deploy/<env>/previous_tag. Only deploy.sh writes them, after a successful rollout of the stable deployment (staging/production modes, and rollback writes current_tag). Canary is never recorded.
sonnet.q7: Stable deployment unchanged and gets all traffic after canary-off; SSM tags unchanged (canary writes none); the migration stays applied (forward-only, safe with the previous image).
sonnet.q8: The older run is stale: the newer run cancels it in step 4 after its smoke tests pass, and the older run also checks at its own checkpoints. Any approval it had does not protect it. The cancellation is recorded in CI, not announced. (Exception: if it already holds the production lock, it is never cancelled.)
sonnet.q9: Outside the window: it checks the clock every minute with no lock held until inside the window (Mon-Thu 09:00-15:00 UTC), then takes the production lock. If another production deploy is in progress, it waits in line for the lock, then redoes stale and window checks; if the window closed it releases the lock and waits for the next window.
sonnet.q10: The canary 5xx ratio (the Prometheus query on shop-api-canary) is measured. The pipeline reads it every 30 s for 15 min. Failure: any reading above 1%, or Prometheus cannot be queried; then canary-off and run fails. No canary traffic (no value) counts as not above 1%.
sonnet.q12: Not by rollback in either case. Staging: if deploy.sh staging fails, no rollback runs, run fails (tags weren't written so rollback would go to the wrong tag). Production: canary-off is run, run fails, no rollback production, and the #deploys message says a person must check the stable deployment; how that person checks/repairs is undecided. The document gives no mechanism to return to a known image.
